title: Bills roster longshots are camp stars at receiver - NewsBreak
text:
Seven different veteran receivers have missed time for the Bills this camp due to injury. That’s half the 14 currently rostered receivers. Even a few of those healthy players are healthy, in part, because they weren’t in Rochester for all of training camp. Simply surviving has given roster longshots like Kristian Wilkerson and Stephen Gosnell a chance. They have taken advantage of the opportunity plenty with repeated attention grabbing receptions. Wilkerson caught a short TD with Brandon Codrington draped all over him Wednesday. There really is no better time to make plays than when teammates are hurting. “Knowing you’re at the bottom of the roster, when guys go down and you can step in, that brings a lot of value,” Wilkerson said.
Wilkerson has played four NFL seasons already with the Raiders and Patriots, plus a 5th season spent entirely on injured reserve. He’s knows how to make a roster even if he’s had to do it as an undrafted player. “It’s not hard when you love football,” Wilkerson said. “Once you prepare for it, it’s the same thing. It’s grass. 53 yards wide. 120 yards long. Just gotta execute when you’re out there.” “He doesn’t say much,” Bills offensive coordinator Joe Brady said. “He just kinda works. He’s a guy that’s been given opportunities and he’s made the most of it. Been very pleased by his movement skills and his knowledge of the offense.”
Gosnell is an undrafted rookie with a good approach towards handling his early success. “A coach always told me you’re only as good as your next practice,” Gosnell said. “That’s the mentality I take every day to practice.” “Steve does everything right,” Brady said. “He knows all the positions. He does his job and is making plays. I’ve loved having him.”
The Bills have long embraced lifting teammates–even the ones who are competing against each other for jobs. Both Wilkerson and Gosnell have been impressed by the culture. “It’s like a brotherhood. Really, the whole team. We’re just tight knit,” Wilkerson said. “There’s no jealousy. We’re all trying to help each other every play. We’re critiquing each other. So, love this group (of receivers).” “Everyone has been real friendly. Just helping you out,” Gosnell said. “When you go somewhere new, you’ve got to earn their respect. The biggest thing for me was earning the respect of the guys and I think I’ve done that.”
Both players are extremely humble, but that doesn’t prohibit the pride earned while turning some heads…. “It’s very exciting and encouraging. That’s what you do it for. You don’t want to not be excited or not be happy about making plays,” Wilkerson said. “I’m very excited, very happy, but I know it’s another day of training camp (camp). You gotta put days together. Stack days together.”
Most professionals know better than to worry all that much about they deserve to make the team or if coaches and management is noticing. At least, they don’t worry about it publicly. Gosnell pointed out a reason why being a part of the Bills gives him even more peace of mind. “This organization wins,” he said. “Obviously, they know how to make good decisions….
